lessons.title: Every Element Is a Box: The Box Model, Lists and Links

objectives.cognitive: Name the four layers of the box model and what list-style-type and the link states change.
objectives.affective: Value pages that give readers room and make every link easy to find.
objectives.psychomotor: Space Juan's section headings and turn his navigation into a list in CodeShare.

blocks.markdown: **How to use this module:** Work in order, Monday to Friday. Run every sample unchanged first, then do its small task. Answer each day's exit slip after its last step.

**Everything happens in CodeShare.** Open your class, then **Module**, this week and a step. **Work in code editor** loads the step's sample files into the editor tabs; **Run code** shows the step's run page in the page window and checks it, and its links open the project's other pages there. It works online and from the classroom laptop; no internet, installation, download or account is needed.

**Reading the outputs:** an output box shows the page text CodeShare checks for the step's run page: the Tab title, the Visible page text, then, on Steps 1, 5 and 9, Media checks. Padding, borders, margins, bullets and link colours are not page text; page checks read them. CSS that puts words on one line or on separate lines (display) or changes letters (text-transform) changes the page text. Spaces count.

**Where we start:** Juan's finished Week 5 site (three pages and styles.css) carries forward in your module project. Each step loads its run page and every file it needs; boxes show only new or changed lines.
**Week 6 starts here:** Juan's site has readable text and a gradient header, but his sections run into each other and his navigation is a plain line of blue links.

blocks.term: The box model, lists and links
blocks.markdown: Every element is a box of four layers, inside out: content (words or a picture), padding (space inside the border), the border (a line around the padding) and margin (space outside, between boxes). A border needs a width, a style and a colour. list-style-type sets each list item's marker (disc, square, upper-roman or none). A link can be styled for each state: :link, :visited, :hover, :focus and :active.
A gift for the class Christmas party: the gift is the content, the crumpled paper around it is padding, the box is the border, and the space between boxes on the table is margin.

**Media steps:** Steps 1, 5 and 9 run index.html, with Juan's picture, sound and video, files your teacher adds under Media files. Online, CodeShare checks them automatically; Run code waits on Loading media… until they are on this device. Offline, these three steps show Checked by your teacher for now, and your teacher presses Mark done. The other steps run projects.html or contact.html and are checked automatically.

blocks.instruction: Juan's Week 5 site carries forward. Every element is a box: content, padding, border, margin. This step gives every h2 a 2px solid maroon line under it (border-bottom), room above that line (padding-bottom: 0.25em) and space above the heading (margin-top: 1.5em), so each section stands apart. Run it unchanged.

lessons.title: Room to Breathe: Padding, Borders, Margins and box-sizing

objectives.cognitive: Explain padding, border and margin values in em and px, and what box-sizing: border-box does to a width.
objectives.affective: Appreciate tidy spacing that helps classmates read and fill in forms.
objectives.psychomotor: Put Juan's nav on one line and give his badges, frame and form boxes padding, borders and margins.

blocks.markdown: **Today's starting point:** Juan's headings have room and his navigation is a list, but each link sits on its own line, and his badges, frame and form boxes use the browser's plain spacing.

One value sets all four sides; two values set top and bottom, then left and right; four go clockwise from the top. padding-bottom or margin-top sets one side. border-style can be solid, dashed or dotted; a border with no style shows nothing. width sets the content's width, so padding and border are added to it, unless box-sizing: border-box counts them inside. Page checks read every size in px: 0.25em of a 24px heading is 6px.

Seats in a jeepney: each passenger (content) has a little room on the seat (padding), the seat's edge is the border, and the space between two passengers is margin, the wider of what each one wants, not both added.

The badges get padding (0.25em top and bottom, 0.5em left and right) and a 1px orange border; the frame gets a solid navy border instead of the browser's grey one, with space above it. blocks.markdown: **Sizes that follow the window or the zoom:** a % width or margin: auto turns into px from the window's size, which differs between screens. The page window also follows your text-size setting, and a border is drawn in whole screen dots, so 2px can read 1.74px. Page checks never read a border's width.

**Practice: margins between two boxes.** A list with margin-bottom: 20px sits above a heading with margin-top: 30px. How much space is between them? Answer: 30px, not 50px: top and bottom margins that meet become one, the larger. Padding never does this.
Answer the Tuesday exit slip now.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between padding and margin?
In Step 4, why is each form box exactly 300px wide with box-sizing: border-box, and 310px without it?
In Step 3, padding: 0.25em on the 12px badges reads 3px. How is this like Week 5's 1.1em label reading 17.6px?
Name the property for (a) space inside the border; (b) space outside the border; (c) the bullet of a list item; (d) a width that includes padding and border. Each correct blank earns 1.25 points.

lessons.title: Bullets and Link States: Styling Lists and Links

objectives.cognitive: Describe list-style-type, list-style-position and the order of the link states :link, :visited, :hover, :active.
objectives.affective: Respect keyboard and mouse users alike by making focus as visible as hover.
objectives.psychomotor: Style Juan's skill lists and links, with link colours that reach 4.5:1.

blocks.markdown: **Today's starting point:** Juan's sections and boxes are spaced, but his lists use the browser's plain bullets and numbers, and his links are still browser blue.

list-style-type: none removes bullets; list-style-position: inside puts the marker inside the box. A CSS list style beats a list's type attribute. Write link states in the order :link, :visited, :focus, :hover, :active (LoVe Fears HAte); Juan writes :focus together with :hover, so keyboard users see it too. A more specific selector wins: nav a:link beats a:link.
A mall directory: the shops are a list, a pointer lights up the shop under your finger like :hover, and shops you already visited could be ticked like :visited.

rows: No: browsers hide it for privacy

No: a check has no mouse

blocks.instruction: List properties change each item's marker. The Skills list gets class="skills": square bullets inside the box, no indent. The next-skills list gets class="next": Roman numbers, so its reversed count reads III, II, I. Run index.html unchanged.

blocks.markdown: **Today's starting point:** Browsers show no error for broken CSS: one missing character can pull a nav bar apart or switch off every rule after it.

A browser skips a value it cannot read and shows no error: a number with no unit (padding: 10), a space before the unit (1.5 em), a misspelt property (pading) or a negative padding. A missing ; skips that declaration and the next one; a missing } switches off every rule after it. When two top and bottom margins meet, only the larger one counts.
A row of jeepney seats held by one bolt: lose the bolt (one ; or }) and the whole row slides off its rail.

performanceTask.title: My Resume, Week 6: Spaced Sections, Styled Lists and a Nav Bar
performanceTask.markdown:
Start Thursday; finish and present Friday. In CodeShare open Projects, then Personal performance-task project. Your Week 5 site carries forward: change your nav into a list on every page and add this week's rules to your own styles.css.

Give your sections padding, a border and margins; give one box with a width box-sizing: border-box; turn your nav into a list of links on one line; style your skills list; write link states in order with colours from the contrast chart. Use only fonts and colours already on the computer: nothing named in url().

Use only safe details: no home address, phone number, birth date, ID numbers or personal social-media accounts. Run code until index.html runs with no error, visit every page with your nav bar, then press Submit this version. Saving or running is not submitting. Pictures, sound and video stay online only (Media files).

Thursday: 0–60 minutes, repairs and the Thursday strip; 60–120 minutes, plan on paper, show the teacher, then start. Friday: 0–30 minutes, finish and run; 30–105 minutes, five-minute presentations; 105–120 minutes, Friday strip and Submit this version.
checklist: Keep your Week 5 site: every page, the frame, the form and styles.css linked from every page.
Give your section headings (or other boxes) padding, a border with a width, style and colour, and a margin.
Give one box that has a width box-sizing: border-box.
Turn your nav into a ul of links on every page, each li on its own line in the code.
Remove the nav list's bullets and indent, and put its items on one line with display: inline-block.
Style your skills list with list-style-type (list-style-position if you like).
Write link states in order: :link, :visited, then :hover with :focus, then :active.
Choose link colours from the chart: 4.5:1 or more in every state, also on your nav bar's background.
Only fonts and colours already on the computer; nothing in url(). No address, phone, birth date, ID numbers or social media.
Run code shows no error; visit every page with your nav bar; press Submit this version, then present.
